title: Fictional Hack Office Emergency Action Plan (exercise only)
disclaimer: Fictional plan for a fictional office used in a simulation exercise. Not a real building's plan, not compliance advice, not certified training. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Red Hat or NVIDIA.

reporting.text: Anyone who sees fire, smoke or a failed door reports it at once. The fastest way to warn the whole building is the nearest manual pull station (move to 'alarm', then pull_alarm): the siren alerts everyone to evacuate but does not say where the hazard is. Use notify to say what you saw and where, citing its evidence ID (e.g. E1); recipient 'all' reaches everyone. Fire spreads, so alert people early. No real emergency call is made in this exercise. Questions go to the warden, Alex.

routes.text: Two ground-level exits lead outside to the assembly point in the south plaza. From the Red Hat room the primary route is door_b -> lobby -> south_branch -> east_exit; alternate: door_a -> north_corridor -> west_exit; from the lobby the alternate is connector -> north_corridor -> west_exit. Interior sliding doors (A, B, connector, south) are electric and can jam shut in a power failure; exits are manual and always open from inside. Fire spreads to nearby floor: never route through or beside known fire, leave early, and if a door or route is reported unavailable, plan a new route before moving. All routes are wheelchair-accessible.

assistance.text: Visitors who may need help agree a buddy in advance. The warden, Alex, is Daniel's designated buddy if Daniel asks for it (Daniel uses a wheelchair; his current preference is in the briefing). Consent first: Daniel asks with request_assistance, Alex goes next to him, then assist links them and they move together on accessible tiles. Using the buddy is good practice but not required: Daniel moves himself and can evacuate independently on accessible routes. Nobody carries or lifts Daniel.

accountability.text: Everyone who gets out goes to the assembly point (yellow area with the flag in the south plaza) and checks in with check_in; it only counts when physically inside the assembly area. Then the warden, Alex, runs verify_roster: every survivor must be checked in. Anyone caught by the fire is reported as lost, never assumed safe. Only the roster verification confirms the exercise complete.
